# stdx/match

> Choosing by value: match x, then case a, b ... else ... end

truck [stdx](../stdx.md) · [source](../../../registry/stdx/match.pkg)

```
match day
case 0, 6
  print "weekend"
case 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
  print "weekday"
else
  print "not a day"
end
```

`x` is evaluated once and compared with `==` to each case's values in
order; the first case with an equal value runs, and no other. With no
match, `else` runs if there is one. Values can be any type `==` takes:
`int`, `u8`, `bool`, `str` (by content) and pointers. `break`,
`continue` and `return` inside a case act on the enclosing loop or
function. Lines between `match` and the first `case` run before the
comparisons.

It expands into an `if` chain, made with `{each}` in the template:

```
do
  let x_ = day
  if false
  elif false || x_ == 0 || x_ == 6
    print "weekend"
  elif false || x_ == 1 || ...
    print "weekday"
  else
    print "not a day"
  end
end
```

## Syntax

Kind: `statement`

```
match {x: expr T} {head: block} [ case {v: args} {then: block} ]* [ else {else: block} ] end
```

| slot | takes | type |
|---|---|---|
| `x` | expression | `T` |
| `head` | block of statements | — |
| `v` (optional) | argument list | — |
| `then` (optional) | block of statements | — |
| `else` (optional) | block of statements | — |

## Expands to

This package has no backend: each use is rewritten to the following
source, with `{slot}` replaced by what was written there, and compiled again.

```
do
let {$x} = {x}
{head}
if false
{each c in case}
elif false{each v in c.v} || {$x} == {v}{end}
{c.then}
{end}
else
{else}
end
end
```
